intro.data: Encode is reversible, and so is Compress. Chain two reversible steps and the whole journey is reversible too — the start and the end are interchangeable.
intro.alchemy: Grind is reversible, and so is Mint. Chain two reversible steps and the whole journey is reversible too — the start and the end are interchangeable.
intro.spellcraft: Etch is reversible, and so is Seal. Chain two reversible steps and the whole working is reversible too — the start and the end are interchangeable.
intro.abstract: f is an isomorphism, and so is h. Chain two isomorphisms and the composite is one too — A and C are interchangeable.

goal.data: Chain the two reversible machines from the start to the goal.
goal.alchemy: Chain the two reversible apparatuses from the start to the goal.
goal.spellcraft: Chain the two reversible runes from the start to the goal.
goal.abstract: Chain the two isomorphisms f and h from A to C.

afterSuccess.data: Two reversible steps in a row make a reversible whole: to undo it, just run Compress backward then Encode backward. So the start and the goal are the same up to renaming.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Two reversible steps in a row make a reversible whole: to undo it, run Mint backward then Grind backward. So the start and the goal are the same up to renaming.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Two reversible steps in a row make a reversible whole: to undo it, run Seal backward then Etch backward. So the start and the goal are the same up to renaming.
afterSuccess.abstract: Two isomorphisms in a row compose to an isomorphism, with inverse f⁻¹ ∘ h⁻¹. So A and C are the same up to renaming.

reveal.summary: Isomorphisms compose: if A ≅ B and B ≅ C then A ≅ C. Being "the same up to renaming" chains together.
notation: A ≅ B  and  B ≅ C  ⟹  A ≅ C
reveal.moreFormal: If f and h are isomorphisms, so is h ∘ f, with inverse f⁻¹ ∘ h⁻¹ (note the reversed order). Isomorphism is therefore an equivalence relation on objects.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: If both steps round-trip, the pipeline round-trips — decode in reverse order.
